knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A ground-level window is cleaned from the top down so runoff does not dry on cleaned glass. Bottom-up cleaning and side-to-side only are not the sequence taught.
A held panel is excluded from the sequence and the exclusion is recorded. It is not cleaned at the end, by hand or with a stronger product.
The product label and safety data sheet govern the dwell time and use of each product. Experience, customer preference or weather alone do not set it.
A quote is tied to the verified scope and states its exclusions. A guaranteed finish at a fixed rate, or a rate that ignores held panels, is not supportable.
Wind and runoff change the conditions, so the worker stops, keeps the public clear and controls the runoff as the job plan requires. Continuing or using more water is not the response.

practicalCriteria: The learner cleans a demonstration panel from the top down and rinses from the top down.
The learner applies the approved product only for the dwell time on the label or safety data sheet.
The learner excludes a held panel from the sequence and records the exclusion.
The learner stops the rinse and controls runoff when the wind changes the conditions.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80% correct (4 of 5). Practical sign-off is assessed separately by observation of a demonstration clean. A knowledge pass does not verify the method in the field.
evidenceRequired: Sequence record with the product and the safety data sheet reference
Time taken per panel or elevation
Held or excluded panels with the reason and decision owner
Quote with verified scope and exclusions
stopWorkCriteria: Product is left on glass beyond the dwell time on the label.
Runoff reaches stormwater or a footpath without control.
A quote is issued with a guaranteed finish for a scope without checking it.
